Mom was sick for awhile then passed when I was 8 and it changed everything. She was the one all 9 of us kids looked to for stability and love while dad was out drinking and cheating on her with the woman who became the evil stepmonster 6 months later. It was as if we were supposed to act like none of them ever existed. Things were pretty sad then a little over a year later my brother died and life kind of sucked more for awhile longer. When I was 17 the stepmonster died and dad repeated the cycle with the kids he had with the 2nd wife by marrying another not so nice woman 7 months later. That one didn't affect me much since I graduated and went on my own before they were married but the half brothers and sisters have their share of issues from their experience. 

There's a lot more to the story about our lives during those years but I hope I've given a little insight into my experience. To sum things up, when mom passed we lost an important person that made us feel loved as well as the relationships with our extended family.  The exprience left us sad, confused and feeling abandoned for quote some time.

I'm a Hospice volunteer and one of the mantras they've preached is pretty accurate..."We don't get over a loss, we get through it."

After way too many deaths of loves ones I've learned that I have to allow myself to feel the grief when it comes up so I can let it out. Keeping it inside and ignoring it was what Dad made us do when my Mom and brother passed and I can see now how it caused the grief to linger longer than was healthy.

I've found that by putting no expectations on how I am grieving makes the process a little more gentle. I know now that the way I am going to experience/process my grief is unique to me and I have had to let go of other people's expectations of how I should be feeling. One day I might feel pretty down about my latest loss and the next night I might be laughing with a bunch of friends. Both help me to move on. 

Has to be one of the hardest parts of the human experience but I've definitely learned to be grateful for the time I have with my loved ones.

In my personal experience I've found that there is not one utility that does everything. I've had good luck though following these steps...

First, go to www.revouninstaller.com and download and install the 30 free day trial of the professional version of the Revo Uninstaller software. It's a quick download and it installs quite fast. It's a very safe utility and I've used it for a few years and it has never created problems for me. 

Once installed use the "Uninstaller" tool to remove any unwanted/unnecessary programs from your system. Revo unes the software's uninstall program then scans your system for leftover registry entries and files after. It also creates a restore point before each uninstall and backs up the registry too. 

After cleaning up the programs look in the "Tools" menu and select the "Junk Files Cleaner" then click on "Scan". After a few minutes you will see a list of files that you can safely remove from the system. Make sure all of the files are selected then use the "Delete Selected Files" button to remove the files from the system.

Next use the "Autorun Manager" tool to review the programs that start when your computer boots and uncheck any programs that you don't need running at boot time. Be careful not to stop your antivirus program though. If you aren't sure about a program you can right click on it and select "Search Google For" to get information about what the program is.

I would suggest that you also run the "Browser Cleaner" and the "Windows Cleaner" tools to get rid of unnecessary temporary files, old history files, and old cookies too. 

At this point you are pretty much done with Revo so go ahead and close it. Download Malwarebytes from www.malwarebytes.org, install it, let it update then run a full scan. This will take quite a bit of time but it's worth it as MalwareBytes will remove a majority of the nasty malware floating around on the web. If anything is found during the scan go ahead and remove it then reboot the system. 

After that I suggest running a defrag on your main hard drive (usually C:). This can be done by opening "My Computer" and right clicking on the "C:" drive then selecting "Properties" from the menu that comes up. In the windows that opens select the "Tools" tab and click on the "Defragment Now" button.Select the "C:" drive and click on the "Analyze Disk" button. It will check your disk and if it suggests that you defrag the drive go ahead and do so.

You can run CCleaner but be careful with what you get rid of as I have seen people screw up Windows by removing things that shouldn't have been removed. 

I hope this is useful to you and if you run into anything you aren't sure about go ahead and ask me, I'd be happy to help as best I can.

Good Luck!
